items.title: Section: Seven Combinations of Affliction, and Killing Worked Out in Full

items.zh: 欲樂者，或有倒想、或無倒想樂所作欲。煩惱者，或貪、或瞋、或癡、或貪瞋、或貪癡、或瞋癡，或貪瞋癡一切皆具。方便究竟者，即於所欲作業隨起方便，或於爾時、或於後時而得究竟。由此五相，於殺生乃至邪見諸業道中，隨其所應，當廣建立圓滿自性十種差別。殺生業道，以有情數眾生為事。若能害者，於眾生所作眾生想，起害生欲，此想即名於彼眾生名不顛倒想。依此想故，作如是心：我當害生。如是名為殺生欲樂。此能害者，或貪所蔽、或瞋所蔽、或癡所蔽、或二所蔽、或三所蔽，而起作心是名煩惱。彼由欲樂及染污心，或自、或他發起方便加害眾生。若害無間彼便命終，即此方便，當於爾時說名成就究竟業道。若於後時彼方捨命，由此方便，彼命終時乃名成就究竟業道。
items.en: The wish is the desire to act arising with either a distorted or an undistorted perception. The affliction is greed, hatred, or delusion, any two together, or all three together. Means and completion is setting into motion the intended karma, reaching completion either at that time or at a later time. The karma-path of killing takes a sentient being as its object. If the one who harms forms the correct perception of the being as that very being, and gives rise to the wish to harm, this perception is called undistorted with respect to that being. Based on this perception, forming the thought, I shall harm this life, is called the wish to kill. This one who harms, obscured by greed, hatred, delusion, two of these, or all three, gives rise to the intention to act, and this is called affliction. Driven by this wish and this defiled mind, whether by one's own hand or through another, one sets in motion the means of harming the being. If, without interruption, that being's life then ends, this very means, at that time, is called the accomplished, complete karma-path. If the being's life ends only later, it is only at that later time, when life ends, that the karma-path is called accomplished and complete.

items.title: Section: Theft, Illicit Conduct, and False Speech Worked Out in Full

items.zh: 不與取業道。事者，謂他所攝物。想者，謂於彼彼想。欲樂者，謂劫盜欲。煩惱者，謂三毒，或具不具。方便究竟者，謂起方便移離本處。欲邪行業道。事者，謂女所不應行；設所應行，非支、非處、非時、非量；若不應理，一切男及不男。想者，於彼彼想。欲樂者，謂樂行之欲。煩惱者，謂三毒，或具不具。方便究竟者，謂兩兩交會。妄語業道。事者，謂見聞覺知，不見、不聞、不覺、不知。想者，謂於見等或翻彼想。欲樂者，謂覆藏想樂說之欲。煩惱者，謂貪瞋癡，或具不具。
items.en: The karma-path of taking what is not given: its object is property belonging to another. Its perception is correct recognition of that object. Its wish is the desire to plunder or steal. Its affliction is the three poisons, complete or incomplete. Its means and completion is setting means into motion and moving the object from its original place. The karma-path of sexual misconduct: its object is a woman not to be approached, or, even where approach is proper, the wrong part, place, time, or measure, or what is improper; and any man or anyone not fully male. Its perception is correct recognition of that person. Its wish is the desire to carry out the act. Its affliction is the three poisons, complete or incomplete. Its means and completion is the union of the two bodies. The karma-path of false speech: its object is seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing, or not seeing, not hearing, not sensing, not knowing. Its perception is correct recognition of what was seen and the rest, or its inversion. Its wish is the desire to conceal and speak falsely. Its affliction is greed, hatred, delusion, complete or incomplete.

items.title: Section: Divisive Speech, Harsh Speech, and the Subtlety of Idle Chatter

items.zh: 方便究竟者，謂時眾及對論者領解。離間語業道。事者，謂諸有情或和不和。想者，謂俱於彼若合若離，隨起一想。欲樂者，謂樂彼乖離，若不和合欲。煩惱者，謂三毒，或具不具。方便究竟者，謂所破領解。麁惡語業道。事者，謂諸有情能為違損。想者，謂於彼彼想。欲樂者，謂樂麁言欲。煩惱者，謂三毒，或具不具。方便究竟者，謂呵罵彼。綺語業道。事者，謂能引發無利之義。想者，謂於彼彼想。欲樂者，謂樂說之欲。煩惱者，謂三毒，或具不具。方便究竟者，謂纔發言。
items.en: Means and completion is that whoever is listening or in dialogue at the time understands what was said; once understood, the karma-path of false speech is accomplished. The karma-path of divisive speech: its object is beings either harmonious or not harmonious. Its perception is forming a single perception of them as either joined or estranged. Its wish is delighting in their estrangement or disharmony. Its affliction is the three poisons, complete or incomplete. Its means and completion is that those broken apart come to understand it. The karma-path of harsh speech: its object is beings capable of being wounded. Its perception is correct recognition of them. Its wish is delighting in harsh speech. Its affliction is the three poisons, complete or incomplete. Its means and completion is scolding them. The karma-path of idle chatter: its object is whatever gives rise to no benefit. Its perception is correct recognition of it. Its wish is delighting in speaking it. Its affliction is the three poisons, complete or incomplete. Its means and completion is simply uttering the words.

items.title: Section: Covetousness, Malice, and Wrong View — The Tenth Karma-Path Complete

items.zh: 貪欲業道。事者，謂屬他財產。想者，謂於彼彼想。欲樂者，謂即如是愛欲。煩惱者，謂三毒，或具不具。方便究竟者，謂於彼事定期屬己。瞋恚業道。事之與想如麁惡語說。欲樂者，謂損害等欲。煩惱者，謂三毒，或具不具。方便究竟者，謂損害等期心決定。邪見業道。事者，謂實有義。想者，謂於有非有想。欲樂者，謂即如是愛欲。煩惱者，謂三毒，或具不具。方便究竟者，謂誹謗決定。復次，殺生有三種。一、有罪增長，二、有罪不增長，三、無有罪。
items.en: The karma-path of covetousness: its object is property belonging to another. Its perception is correct recognition of it. Its wish is this very craving. Its affliction is the three poisons, complete or incomplete. Its means and completion is firmly resolving that it belongs to oneself. The karma-path of malice: its object and perception are as with harsh speech. Its wish is the desire to harm and the like. Its affliction is the three poisons, complete or incomplete. Its means and completion is firmly resolving the intent to harm. The karma-path of wrong view: its object is what genuinely exists. Its perception is regarding what exists as not existing. Its wish is this very craving. Its affliction is the three poisons, complete or incomplete. Its means and completion is a settled conviction that denies it. Moreover, killing is of three kinds. First, killing whose fault increases. Second, killing whose fault does not increase. Third, killing without fault.

items.title: Section: Killing With Increasing Fault, Without Increasing Fault, and Without Fault — and Covetousness's Five Aspects

items.zh: 生罪因緣，亦略有三。一、煩惱所起，二、能生於苦，三、希望滿足。初具三緣；次有二種，無希望滿；後唯生苦。復次，略由五相，建立貪欲、瞋恚、邪見圓滿自相。何等名為貪欲五相？一、有耽著心，謂於自財所。二、有貪婪心，謂樂積財物。三、有饕餮心，謂於屬他資財等事計為華好，深生愛味。四、有謀略心，謂作是心：凡彼所有，何當屬我。五、有覆蔽心，謂貪欲纏之所覆故，不覺羞恥，不知過患及與出離。
items.en: The conditions generating fault are, in brief, also three. First, arising from affliction. Second, generating suffering. Third, the satisfaction of one's wish. The first kind possesses all three conditions; the second kind possesses two, without the satisfaction of the wish; the last possesses only the generation of suffering. Moreover, in brief, by five aspects, the complete own-mark of covetousness, malice, and wrong view is established. What are the five aspects of covetousness? First, a mind of attachment, towards one's own wealth. Second, a mind of greed, delighting in accumulating wealth. Third, a mind of gluttony, regarding another's wealth as beautiful, generating deep craving and relish for it. Fourth, a mind of scheming, thinking: whatever belongs to another, how might it come to belong to me? Fifth, a mind of obscuration, covered over by the entangling grip of covetousness, so that one feels no shame, and recognises neither the fault involved nor any need to escape it.

items.zh: 設於自財有耽著心，無餘心現，當知此非圓滿貪欲意惡行相。如是有耽著心及貪婪心，無餘心現，亦非圓滿貪欲之相。如是廣說，乃至如前所說諸相隨闕一種，即非圓滿貪欲之相。若全分攝，乃名圓滿貪欲之相。

blocks.text: Each of the ten courses of action analysed through the same five factors.
Master Cháng Bǎi: one who means to kill A, and confirms the person is A, has an undistorted perception; only when the being dies is the path of killing complete.
Master Cháng Bǎi: with the thought of stealing, moving the thing from its place is theft.
Master Cháng Bǎi: harsh speech is complete once spoken, whether or not the other understands; idle chatter is complete on being uttered.
What the mind covets is held as surely its own. Wrong view: regarding what truly exists, such as the Three Jewels and the four truths, as not existing, and clinging firmly to that.

Master Cháng Bǎi: if the wish to kill is satisfied, with gladness, the fault increases; if one regrets or fails, it does not. A bodhisattva killing out of compassion to save others is discussed separately (Days 361–362). Others' wealth seems beautiful, and the covetous mind relishes it, never satisfied. (Untranslated, 0631a06: if any one of the listed marks is missing, covetousness is not complete.)
"If one regrets, the fault does not increase." Regret is not useless; it changes the weight of what was done.

quiz.q: What are killing's object and undistorted perception, and when is it complete?
options: all things; perceiving non-being; complete on striking, whenever the other dies
only humans; complete on the thought
only animals; complete on speaking
a sentient being; perceiving the being as such; complete when life ends
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one who means to kill A, confirming the person is A, has an undistorted perception; only when the being dies is the path of killing complete. If it dies later, completion comes later. The English follows this.

quiz.q: What are taking what is not given's object and completion?
options: ownerless things; completion being using or selling it
what another owns, sentient or not; moving it from its place
community goods; carrying them out
gold; the thought alone
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the object is what another holds, whether sentient or not; the Dharma is strict: with the thought of stealing, moving the thing from its place is theft. 處 can be land, space, a bridge, or a boat. The English is accurate.

quiz.q: The English has "and, where unfitting, any man or person of indeterminate sex." What is the problem?
options: no problem: the phrase limits the following words to unfitting cases, 不男 meaning indeterminate sex, as the lecture says
two separate items are merged into a condition, and 不男 is not "indeterminate sex"
the problem is "part"
the problem is "measure"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi puts "not according with reason" alongside wrong part, place, and time, within what applies to a proper partner; men and 不男 are a separate item, and §41 says they are not to be approached in any case. The English conditional makes these only conditionally wrong.

quiz.q: Is §35's "Means and completion is that whoever is listening..." treatise text? What of the English?
options: yes: all of §35 is the treatise's wording, the English being literal and citable, the lecture merely reading it aloud
no: it is the lecturer's wording, the treatise saying the audience and interlocutor understand; the English follows the paraphrase
no: from the Great Perfection commentary
no: from the Vinaya
quiz.why: The source reads that means and completion is the audience and interlocutor understanding. Master Cháng Bǎi's paraphrase replaced it in the Chinese, and the English translates the paraphrase. Doctrinally the point stands: the lie is complete once understood. The source line, however, should be restored.

quiz.q: When are divisive, harsh, and idle speech complete?
options: divisive: those split understand; harsh: on scolding; idle: on speaking
all require real harm: actual split, actual anger, and belief, without which there is no path, as the lecture stresses
all must be written
all need witnesses
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with harsh speech, whether or not the other understands, once the scolding is spoken it is complete; idle chatter is complete on being uttered; divisive speech seeks to split people whether harmonious or not. Its completion in the treatise is understanding by those split.

quiz.q: What is the completion of covetousness and malice?
options: actually obtaining it; actually striking
on speaking
the first thought
firmly resolving it is one's own; firmly resolving to harm
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: what the mind covets, whether person or thing, is held as surely to be one's own; once the mind is determined to harm, the means and completion are already there. So mental paths complete inwardly, without any bodily act.

quiz.q: The English has "firmly resolving to slander it." What is the problem?
options: no problem: wrong view requires resolving to tell others, inner views not counting, as the lecture says
the problem is "firmly"
the problem is "it"
completion is inward firm denial; the English reads as resolving to speak, a prelude to speech
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: regarding what really exists, such as the Three Jewels and the four truths, denying it and giving rise to a firm clinging is called this; if slander is spoken out of wrong view, it falls under heavy idle chatter. So completion is inner conviction, not a resolve to speak.

quiz.q: What are wrong view's object and perception?
options: what really exists; regarding what is as not being
what is false; taking the absent as present
another's wealth; correct perception
beings; joined or estranged
quiz.why: The object of wrong view is real, and the perception denies it. Master Cháng Bǎi: regarding what truly exists as not existing, such as the Three Jewels and four truths. Thus this path is the negating kind of wrong view, a point that returns at §46.

quiz.q: How do the three kinds of killing match the three conditions for fault?
options: increase has only affliction; non-increase two; faultless all three, bodhisattvas having affliction and satisfaction too
all three have all three
fault that increases has all three; non-increasing lacks satisfaction; faultless only generates suffering
none has any
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if the wish to kill is satisfied, with gladness, fault increases; if one regrets or fails, no satisfaction; a bodhisattva killing out of compassion to save others lacks greed, hatred, and delusion, yet the other suffers. The English is accurate.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain gluttonous and obscured minds among covetousness's aspects?
options: gluttony concerns only food, and obscuration hiding wealth
both wholesome
relishing others' wealth, always wanting more; covered by greed, feeling no shame
both of hatred
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: others' wealth seems beautiful and the mind relishes it like a glutton, never satisfied; covered by greed one feels no shame. The English "recognises neither the fault involved nor any need to escape it" is good. The source's sentence on completeness is missing from the English.
